senses.note: The proper name, four consonants. Left untranslated because it is a NAME, not a title — the same reason Moses is not rendered by its meaning. Substituting "the LORD" is what the reading tradition did, and it hides that a name is present. The scrolls treat it as special: 11Q5 writes it in paleo-Hebrew inside an otherwise square-script text.

unresolved: Original vocalisation is not recoverable; the pointing in the Masoretic text belongs to a different word read in its place.
